_comment: Phase 9. Second registered DrugSim endpoint (Metabolism category), following the exact registry shape established for herg_inhibition_v1.json. File-based substitute for a real model registry DB row, same limitation already documented there.

final_report_status_history.note: Promotion decision made on first evaluation -- see report Sec 'Final Decision' for full reasoning (baselines clearly beaten, reliability layer verified functioning, genuinely independent external validation confirms internal test performance).

endpoint.name: CYP3A4 inhibition
endpoint.definition: label=1 (inhibitor) if aggregated IC50 <= 10000 nM (10 uM), else label=0 (non-inhibitor)
endpoint.threshold_note: 10 uM is a literature convention for a binary CYP-inhibition-risk call (comparable order of magnitude to published in vitro DDI-risk screening cutoffs), not a universal biological constant -- same convention class already used for hERG.
endpoint.target: ChEMBL CHEMBL340, Cytochrome P450 3A4, Homo sapiens, SINGLE PROTEIN
endpoint.category: Metabolism (ADMET) -- the platform's first endpoint outside the existing Toxicity category (hERG)

dataset.source: ChEMBL REST API (direct), CHEMBL340 IC50/nM activities, complete population not a sample (12,359 raw records)
dataset.impossible_value_note: One entity (aggregated IC50 = 0 nM) traced to a single ChEMBL record flagged 'Outside typical range'; that validity flag was added to this endpoint's exclusion filter (not retrofitted onto hERG, which is left unchanged per Phase 9's explicit constraint) -- see docs/phase9/phase9-admet-expansion-report.md.

features.note: feature_set_id is IDENTICAL to herg_inhibition_v1.json's -- expected and correct: this is a content address over the descriptor/fingerprint/standardisation/RDKit-version TOOLCHAIN (ADR-005), which both endpoints share unmodified. It is not a per-dataset identifier.

validation_strategy.split_method: Global scaffold-level split_group (ADR-009): sha256(scaffold_key || split_salt) mod 10, deterministic, split_salt='cyp3a4_inhibition_v1' (independent of hERG's split assignment)
validation_strategy.leakage_prevention: One row per standardised entity (inchikey_full) by construction -- no duplicate structures possible. Split-group assignment is a pure deterministic function of scaffold key, asserted 1:1 in prepare_features.py (a scaffold key mapping to >1 split_group raises immediately).

benchmark_split_random_proxy.note: random-split proxy, not a true TDC canonical split -- none exists for this ChEMBL-sourced dataset

metrics.gap_explanation: Global scaffold splitting prevents cross-dataset/near-neighbour leakage; the gap is the leakage the scaffold split removes.
metrics.comparison_to_herg: hERG's own registered global-split test metrics (roc_auc=0.7875, balanced_accuracy=0.6495) are directly comparable to CYP3A4's (0.7995, 0.652) -- CYP3A4's discriminative performance is at parity with, not meaningfully weaker than, the platform's existing validated endpoint.
metrics.known_limitation: Specificity (0.4052) is the weakest metric: the model over-calls 'inhibitor', consistent with the 67% positive training prevalence and CYP3A4's broad substrate promiscuity making the non-inhibitor chemical space harder to characterise than hERG's more specific channel-blocking motif. See error_analysis_report.json.

external_validation.dataset: TDC CYP3A4_Veith (PubChem AID 1851 qHTS primary screen, Veith et al. 2009 Nat Biotechnol)
external_validation.retrieval_method: Direct HTTP fetch of the underlying Harvard Dataverse file -- PyTDC's own Python package failed in this environment (returned an HTML error page), same limitation Phase 3 documented for TDC access generally.
external_validation.label_definition_caveat: TDC's Y label is PubChem's own qHTS active/inactive call, a different operationalisation of CYP3A4 inhibition than this model's aggregated-IC50-based definition -- some disagreement is expected from label-definition differences alone, not only model error.
external_validation.conclusion: ROC-AUC (0.7758) and balanced accuracy (0.7022) on a genuinely independent 12,152-compound dataset with a different label-generation methodology are consistent with (specificity/balanced-accuracy: better than) internal scaffold-split test performance -- real evidence against overfitting to ChEMBL-specific idiosyncrasies, not merely a re-split of the same data.

components: max Tanimoto similarity to training set (Morgan fingerprints)
k-NN distance in standardised descriptor space (k=5, threshold=95th percentile of training-internal distances)
applicability_domain_method.verdict_logic: out_of_domain if max_tanimoto<0.4 OR >=2 of {max_tanimoto<0.6, knn_dist>p95_train, scaffold_not_in_training} triggered; borderline if exactly 1; else in_domain
applicability_domain_method.empirical_validation: 2-signal verdict (scaffold excluded, tautologically triggered on any scaffold-holdout test set): in_domain accuracy 82.8% (n=262), borderline 69.9% (n=93), out_of_domain 52.9% (n=104) -- clean monotonic degradation confirms the AD carries real, usable signal for this endpoint too.
applicability_domain_method.caveat: 3-signal in_domain verdict is 0/459 on this test set by construction (scaffold-holdout guarantees scaffold_not_in_training=True for every held-out compound); only reachable for a real query compound whose scaffold is already in the training pool.

uncertainty_method.nonconformity_score: 1 - predicted probability of the candidate class
uncertainty_method.calibration_set: split_group 7 (n=514), used for the first and only time in reliability.py

uncertainty_tracks_error.conclusion: Confident (singleton) predictions are substantially more accurate than genuinely uncertain ones -- the uncertainty signal is functioning as intended, not decorative.

post_hoc_calibration_evaluated.recommendation: use raw predict_proba -- neither Platt nor isotonic post-hoc calibration improved on it, same conclusion as hERG

error_analysis_summary.dominant_error_mode: false positives (model over-calls inhibitor), consistent with low specificity
error_analysis_summary.representative_pattern: largest errors cluster among non-inhibitors with true IC50 just above the 10 uM threshold (14-25 uM range) -- consistent with genuine difficulty near a hard threshold applied to a continuous potency measure, not a data-pipeline defect
error_analysis_summary.assay_variability_check: single-measurement compounds (74.9% accuracy) outperformed multiply-measured compounds (62.5%) -- opposite of the 'more measurements = cleaner label' hypothesis; plausibly explained by multiply-studied compounds tending to be pharmacologically borderline/interesting rather than by aggregation noise

reasoning: Meaningfully and substantially beats all three required baselines (majority-class, descriptor-only logistic regression, descriptor-only random forest) -- +0.058 ROC-AUC over the strongest baseline.
Discriminative performance (0.7995 ROC-AUC, scaffold-split test) is at parity with the platform's existing VALIDATED hERG model (0.7875), not a weaker standard applied to pass a new endpoint.
Applicability domain shows the required monotonic reliability degradation (82.8% -> 69.9% -> 52.9% accuracy from in-domain to out-of-domain) -- the AD signal is real and usable, not decorative.

Conformal uncertainty achieves empirical coverage (89.76%) within tolerance of its 90% nominal target, AND confident predictions are demonstrably more accurate than uncertain ones (83.7% vs 56.1%) -- the uncertainty layer functions as intended.

A genuinely independent external validation set (12,152 disjoint compounds, different label-generation methodology, zero influence on any modelling decision) shows CONSISTENT, in some metrics BETTER, performance than the internal test set -- strong evidence against overfitting.
documented_limitations_carried_by_this_s: Specificity (0.4052 internal / higher externally at 0.61-equivalent) is the weakest metric -- the model has a real, asymmetric tendency to over-predict 'inhibitor'. Any UI surfacing this prediction must show this alongside the reliability/uncertainty information, never as a bare label.
The 10 uM inhibitor threshold is a literature convention, not a clinical or regulatory boundary -- errors concentrate near this boundary, as expected for any hard threshold on a continuous measure.

External validation used a differently-labelled dataset (qHTS single-concentration screen vs. aggregated dose-response IC50) -- consistency is reassuring but not a perfect apples-to-apples confirmation.

Endpoint covers CYP3A4 inhibition ONLY -- says nothing about other CYP isoforms, other metabolic pathways, or actual clinical drug-drug-interaction risk, which depends on additional pharmacokinetic factors (dose, exposure, other enzyme/transporter involvement) this model does not model.

code_version.git_commit: unavailable in this environment (no git history check performed for this value; hERG's registry entry recorded one from an environment where `git rev-parse` was run -- not repeated here to avoid fabricating a commit hash)

artifact.note: gitignored binary, not committed, same convention as hERG's artifact.
artifact.reproducibility: regenerate via: fetch_chembl_data.py -> build_dataset.py -> prepare_features.py -> train.py, in order, RANDOM_SEED=42 fixed throughout; exact byte-identical retraining is NOT guaranteed since fetch_chembl_data.py re-queries a live external API that can gain new records over time (same documented limitation as hERG).

inference_support._comment: Frozen conformal calibration + AD reference data exported by models/admet/cyp3a4_inhibition/10_export_inference_support.py -- never recomputed at inference time.
